chain.fact: The function initializes error=EACCES. Audit-token path and guest acquisition precede stage kernel-image-validity. SecCodeCheckValidity uses kSecCSNoNetworkAccess with a NULL additional requirement; failure preserves its OSStatus and returns the preselected EACCES.

plain mode bypasses the image gate. For baseline the image gate occurs before CopyPath completion, reopening/stat/hash, match decision, adversarial mutation or resume. The recorded stage identifies this validity refusal, not a writer mutation failure.

compiler-default binaries are compiled without an explicit signing command. Darwin retains plain and baseline for this variant. Separate copied binaries are explicitly ad-hoc signed as adhoc-test-only and receive the additional mutation schedules.
The plain case requires successful execution and original output. The non-plain baseline still requires errno=0; the passive witness diagnostic cannot replace that assertion.
errSecCSUnsigned is -67062; this classifies the observed Security OSStatus as unsigned code.
CheckValidity validates the signature and dynamic code state. NULL removes additional requirement predicates; it does not disable signature validation.
CopyPath returns a disk location. CopySigningInformation can inspect unsigned code, but does not by itself replace successful validity checking or establish the same running-code/disk relationship.

rejectedAsUnjustified: Ignoring errSecCSUnsigned or deleting CheckValidity removes an existing witness guard without an equivalent byte-consumption proof.
Explicitly signing compiler-default or skipping its baseline changes the original fixture/acceptance scope.
CopyPath or CopySigningInformation alone is not the same image proof.
This finding does not authorize rejecting existing unsigned/custom sources or scripts, trusting writers, silent copying, or changing permissions.
